title: Workload stratification harness for quantization profiles: slice-based regression detection & p95-aware sampling
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a repeatable, low-noise benchmarking harness that stratifies production-like workloads into statistically meaningful slices to evaluate quantization profiles (FP16 / INT8 / INT4 and hybrid mixes). The harness should produce tokens/sec and latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), associate quality deltas against reference outputs, and run continuous regression detection with automated alerting and canary rollback hints.
acceptance_criteria: H1: Harness can replay representative request traces partitioned into at least 6 slices (seq-length buckets, prompt type, cache-hit vs cold-start, user intent) with deterministic seed control.

H2: For each quant profile (fp16,int8,int4,mixed) generate throughput (tokens/sec), tail latency (p95), and quality metrics (token-level perplexity delta, BLEU/ROUGE on eval sets or model-score delta) in a single run.

H3: Regression detector operating on p95 and reference-quality metrics with configurable thresholds (absolute and relative) and EWMA/CUSUM baseline drift signals; false alarm rate < 2% on historical holdout traces.

H4: Results persisted to our benchmarking dashboard schema and provide per-slice CSV export plus a human-readable summary report and recommended rollback / fallback model variant when regressions detected.
H5: Test config is parameterized and runnable from CI (k8s job) and locally via docker-compose for debugging.
H6: End-to-end latency measurements are reproducible within ±5% over repeated runs for stable slices (no upstream load variance).
H7: README and runbook created with instructions for adding new slices and tuning detector thresholds.
test_configuration: Workload trace source: production sampling pipeline (1% sample anonymized) and synthetic prompt generator for corner cases.
Slice definitions: seq_len_0_64, seq_len_65_256, seq_len_257_1024, cache_hot, cache_cold, multimodal_stub.
Batching policies: target latency SLO 150ms p95, batching window 5ms/10ms/20ms experimented.
Quant profiles: fp16 baseline, int8-opt, int4-safe (with fallback-to-int8 on layer-level score drop), mixed-per-layer configs.
Runtime: dedicated test pool of gpus (A100-40GB equivalent), pinned kernel selection disabled/enabled for experiments.
Metrics emitted: tokens/sec, per-request latency histogram, p50/p95/p99, mem usage, kernel-run time, perplexity delta to fp16 reference, BLEU/ROUGE on labeled eval subset.
Detector settings: EWMA alpha=0.2, CUSUM k=0.5, h thresholds configurable per-metric and per-slice.
Duration per run: full-sweep ~4 hours on target pool, mini-sweep (smoke) ~20 minutes.
Seed control: deterministic random seeds for prompt generator and sampling, recorded in run metadata.
Data retention: raw logs + CSV per-run persisted for 90 days in benchmark-bucket.
Canaries: automated canary rollout script that suggests a fallback model variant and generates rollback PR template.
schedule: Phase 1: infra + slice definitions (1 week). Phase 2: run full sweep with current profiles and tune detector (1 week). Phase 3: iterate on mixed-precision fallback heuristics and integrate with canary automation (1 week).
results_summary: Initial smoke runs show expected ordering: fp16 highest quality and p95 around 120ms for mid-length slices; int8 reduces p95 by ~18% and tokens/sec improves ~22% with median perplexity delta +0.6%. Int4 aggressive profile achieves ~2.1x tokens/sec vs fp16 on small sequences but exhibits a bimodal quality distribution: 92% of prompts within acceptable delta, 8% with large deltas concentrated in math/code prompt slices. Detector configuration with EWMA+CUSUM successfully highlighted two int4 regressions on the code-samples slice with confidence > 0.9 and low false positives on holdout traces.
notes_and_discussion: 03-01: Ran initial full-sweep. Observed int4 failures correlate with per-layer outlier activations on early transformer layers; hypothesis: quantization calibration using per-channel min-max is insufficient for these kernels.
03-02: Design decision: implement lightweight per-layer fallback to int8 when per-layer quality score crosses threshold, rather than full-model fallback to preserve throughput gains.
03-02: Discussed threshold tuning with SRE; agreement to expose per-slice thresholds so product teams can opt-in to stricter quality constraints for customer-facing slices.
03-03: Marco pushed branch with slicebench harness and deterministic seeding (PR #4492). Awaiting review from infra and reliability.
03-03: QA asked for clearer failure-mode logging (payloads redacted) to triage quality regressions faster; added to next steps.
Operational note: When running against shared dedicated pool, enable capacity tagging to avoid interference from other experiments.

Trade-off call: Increase of detector sensitivity reduces missed regressions but raises engineering noise; propose initial sensitivity tuned towards low false-positive rate, then ramp up for high-risk releases.
Open question: Do we store per-slice calibration artifacts for quick re-eval or recompute calibration on each run? Storage cost vs reproducibility trade-off.
Suggested archival scheme: Keep calibration artifacts for release-tagged runs and recompute for ad-hoc sweeps.
Link to benchmarking dashboard prototype: dashboards/quant-slice-2025Q1 (internal).
